name: Neck fillers / skin boosters

lead: Neck fillers and skin boosters are injectable treatments, typically hyaluronic acid, aimed at horizontal neck lines and skin quality.
The sources found are clinical-trial registrations, including a 26-person Restylane Refyne neck study, without published results to summarise.

paras: A gel is injected into or beneath the skin by a clinician to add volume or hydration to creased areas.
Risks were not described in the sources reviewed. Fillers are administered by clinicians, and product regulation varies by country.

lead: Neck fillers and skin boosters are injectable treatments, usually hyaluronic acid products, used to soften horizontal neck lines and improve neck skin quality. In looksmaxxing and aesthetic-medicine discussion they are an option for horizontal neck rhytides, sometimes called necklace lines.

Published human evidence found for this entry is limited to registered trials. A registered study (NCT04162496) evaluated Restylane Refyne for correcting horizontal neck rhytides in 26 participants and is listed as completed [1]. Another registered study evaluated a hyaluronic acid-based filler, NCTF135HA, for anti-aging performance and tolerance in 146 participants [2]. A registered trial combined Ultherapy with Sculptra for skin laxity [3].

paras: Three registered trials are relevant. NCT04162496 tested Restylane Refyne for horizontal neck rhytides, 26 participants, completed [1]. NCT05609617 evaluated NCTF135HA, a hyaluronic acid-based filler, for aging signs and tolerance, 146 participants, completed [2]. NCT01422538 studied Ultherapy after Sculptra treatment for skin laxity, 30 participants, completed [3]. The registry entries consulted here did not provide published efficacy results in the material reviewed, so effect sizes are not summarised.
Neck fillers are a minor topic in appearance communities compared with jaw and chin procedures. No forum material on them was found in the sources reviewed.
